_what: Windows `.cmd` shims -- three generated by npm's own generator, one hand-written.
_how: The generated three: node -e "import cmdShim from '<npm>/node_modules/cmd-shim/lib/index.js'; await cmdShim(<target>, <bin>)" against npm 11's bundled cmd-shim, macOS, 2026-09-11. A .cmd shim is the shape every npm install of `claude`/`copilot` produces on Windows, and it is what `shutil.which` resolves there.
_why: tests/test_windows_launch.py parses these on whatever OS the suite is running on. Recording the generator's real output means the parser is tested against the artifact rather than against somebody's memory of it.
_measured_on_a_runner: acceptance run 34613046096, windows-latest, 2026-09-11: `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` produced `C:\npm\prefix\claude.CMD` with **no JavaScript in it at all** (`npm view @anthropic-ai/claude-code bin` -> `{claude: 'bin/claude.exe'}` at 2.1.268 -- the npm package installs a native launcher), while `@github/copilot` produced a shim running `node_modules\@github\copilot\npm-loader.js`. Both shapes are here because both are real.

claude.cmd.note: the plain `node` shebang shape -- what an npm package with a JavaScript bin produces, and what earlier claude-code versions installed. The doubled space before the quoted target is the generator's own (`"%_prog%" ${args} ${target}` with an empty `args`).

claude-native.cmd.note: **the shape a Windows runner actually has for `claude` today.** No shebang, so npm writes a shim that runs the target directly: there is no JavaScript entry point to find, and the right answer is to launch that executable rather than the batch file that wraps it.

copilot.cmd.note: npm copies the target's shebang flags into the shim, so the launcher has to carry them too -- starting the program without them would be starting it differently from the way its own installer does. The real `copilot.CMD` on the runner names `npm-loader.js` instead of `index.js`; same shape, and the parser reads the name rather than knowing it.

hand-written-python.cmd.note: hand-written, not npm's -- the shape `tests/_fake_cli.py` writes for this repository's own fake CLIs. It names neither JavaScript nor an executable, so it is the fallback case: launch the shim as a batch file and say so in the launch log.
